_provenance.data: StudyENG1c Part D FIT pairs only (240 pairs in the record, 360 trials built)
_provenance.derived: DERIVED and FIT. Per-request step membership is not recorded by StudyENG1c; every per-piece engine time here is derived by StudyENG1d's attribution method (first scheduled time = client first-token time minus the plugin's prefill_time; prefill end = the last step row at or before the client first-token time). StudyENG1e-chain measures the membership directly. All pairs are StudyENG1c Part D FIT pairs; no HOLDOUT pair is read.

awaiting_eng1e.encoder_budget_per_step: Whether the extra step per piece is forced by an encoder or multimodal input budget rather than the token budget. Part A cannot separate the two.
awaiting_eng1e.in_step_merge_rule: Whether, and under what admission condition, a background prefill joins a step a piece is already prefilling in. Part A shows the engine does co-schedule (median 3,780 and 3,402 other prefill tokens inside the pieces' own steps, max ctx_req 2), but the per-step composition is DERIVED by subtraction, not measured per request.
awaiting_eng1e.step_granularity_tokens_per_step: How many NEW tokens of a multimodal piece the engine actually puts in one step. Part A derives 1.75 steps per piece for piece1024 and 1.92 for piece2048 against pol4's 1.0, but the derivation cannot say WHICH tokens went in which step. StudyENG1e's per-step request membership measures it.

inherits.why: StudyPOL5 section 2 fitted the image-aware front end on 58,085 idle and 12,261 busy measured windows from StudyENG1d FIT and StudyENG1 Part C FIT rows, R^2 0.985. The brief authorises its use for the piece gap representation.

model: pol6 (NOT adopted, NOT frozen; pol4 remains the frozen and default model)

but_pol4_already_has_them.reading: pol4 prices a front-end window per request from body size, so its own simulation already contains inter-piece gaps and already schedules background work inside them. It does not treat the chain as contiguous.

partA_verdict.erratum: ERRATUM 2026-11-17 (addendum, section 11): the clause that pol4 never merges a background prefill into a piece's step is WRONG. It was inferred from reading `_schedulable` and never measured. Measured from pol4's own step log, pol4 shares 54.98 % of chained piece1024 steps and 69.31 % of piece2048 steps with a background prefill, MORE often than the engine does, and admits up to 6, 8 and 21 prefills into one step against the engine's observed maximum of 2. StudyPOL5 section 1.5 was right. The granularity and step-duration findings are unaffected and the mechanism is restated as H-overmerge.

gaps_are_real.reading: the gap is real and is almost entirely the NEXT piece's front-end window; every gap that contains a step boundary at all carries other work, so the engine does serve background requests in the gaps

partA_verdict.hypothesis: H-gap: a model that treats a chain as contiguous occupancy over-charges background requests for blocking that did not happen in the inter-piece gaps.

leading_alternative.name: H-granularity with H-overmerge

negative_control_mono11k.reading: a monolithic 11k rebuild exceeds the step budget, so it runs ALONE (zero other prefill tokens in its steps, max ctx_req 1) and pol4 gets its step count right (2.0 against 2.0). Its over-prediction ratio is 1.13, the smallest of the three actions. The mechanism that is absent for mono is exactly the one Part A names for the pieces.

leading_alternative.statement: pol4 gets a chain's total wall-clock span right and its step structure wrong. It models a piece as ONE long step; the engine really spreads a piece over about 1.8 shorter steps. pol4 also merges background prefills into a piece's step MORE often than the engine does (54.98 % and 69.31 % of piece steps against a derived 40 % and 48 %) and admits up to 6, 8 and 21 prefills into one step against the engine's observed maximum of 2, so every merged request is charged that over-long step's duration. The error is therefore over-merging into an over-long step, not a missing merge.

statement_erratum.was: pol4 gets a chain's total wall-clock span right and its step structure wrong. It models a piece as ONE long step; the engine really spreads a piece over about 1.8 shorter steps and co-batches background prefill into them. A background request arriving mid-prefill therefore waits in pol4 for the end of one long step instead of the end of one short step, and can never be merged into the piece's own step.
statement_erratum.why: the clause that a background request can never be merged into the piece's own step was inferred from reading `_schedulable` and never measured. pol4 merges on 54.98 % of chained piece1024 steps and 69.31 % of piece2048 steps, more often than the engine does. StudyPOL5 section 1.5 was right.

leading_alternative.what_would_settle_it: StudyENG1e's per-step request membership: it names which requests were in each step, so the step count per piece and the merge rule are measured rather than derived by subtraction.

partA_verdict.verdict: CONTRADICTED on StudyENG1c Part D FIT as an explanation of the over-prediction

where_the_over_prediction_is.reading: 89 % of the over-prediction (270.5 s of 303.9 s) is carried by background requests whose first token lands while the engine IS prefilling a piece, not in a gap (31.3 s, 10 %). The error is in the with-arm prediction (+265.1 s) and not the without-arm (-5.4 s).
where_the_over_prediction_is.unit: TTFT-sum seconds, summed over all 161 chained FIT trials

partB.fit_set: StudyENG1e FIT only, 15 of 20 trials per cell, both injection modes

rejected_on_fit.reason: not an error: the engine runs every piece in ONE step, median and max 1.0 in all 16 chain cells, which is what pol4 already does
implemented and rejected: forbidding a piece to share its step with background prefill moved the chain ratio from 1.636 to 1.897 on FIT
not an error: StudyENG1e's encoder check passed in every cell

measured_handover_window.status: MEASURED on StudyENG1e FIT, REJECTED by the regression gate, NOT adopted
measured_handover_window.what_it_is: the window from a piece completing to the next piece being added to the engine (StudyENG1e gaps.fe_next_s, which equals its fe_later_s exactly), per body kind and measured piece size
measured_handover_window.why_rejected: it corrects criterion (i) (latency 0.5944 to 0.8472, TTFT 0.8139 to 0.9083) but worsens criterion (iii) from 0.0209 to 0.1460, because pol4 reproduces a chain's own span only through two errors that cancel in it: the piece step is 1.06 to 1.62x too long and the hand-over window is 3 to 13x too short
